body: The Hawaii Supreme Court, in an opinion by Justice Ginoza, reviewed the dismissal of a suit by Haleiwa Town Center, LLC, which leases the Haleiwa Town Center from the Trustees of the Estate of Bernice Pauahi Bishop, also known as Kamehameha Schools. According to the opinion, the tenant's First Amended Complaint alleges that the landlord tried to shift its kuleana access obligations onto the tenant, made conflicting representations about whether a historic lane was on the tenant's property, and encroached on the tenant's property during construction. The only lease provision the complaint relies on is the quiet enjoyment provision. The Supreme Court said the trial court was required to accept the allegations as true and held that the complaint asserts viable claims for breach of contract and breach of the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing.

The Supreme Court held that the tenant's unfair competition claim was properly dismissed. It also held that the Circuit Court should have allowed the tenant to file its proposed Second Amended Complaint, which adds factual allegations supporting the two surviving claims.

On fees, the court held that because there is no prevailing party at this stage, the Intermediate Court of Appeals erred by vacating the Circuit Court's denial of the landlord's request for fees and costs and by awarding the landlord fees and costs on appeal. The court vacated the appeals court's judgment in part and remanded the case to the Circuit Court.

timeline.label: Tenant files its First Amended Complaint against the landlord
Circuit Court grants the landlord's motion to dismiss
Hawaii Supreme Court holds two of the tenant's three claims viable, leaves the unfair competition claim dismissed, and remands
